title: Supported function effects remain within authored effect policy
statement: When a Function Contract authors an effect policy, every supported direct and transitive function effect MUST belong to that policy's allowed effect set.
rationale: A function can preserve nominal and value-domain correctness while unexpectedly mutating receiver state, interacting externally, panicking, or reaching unsafe execution through a resolved callee.
failure_prevented: Supported direct or transitive mutation and effect behavior escaping the function-level policy that downstream engineering intent relies upon.
applicability: Functions with an authored Function Contract v3/v4 effect policy. Function Contract v3 external_interaction is an explicit compatibility umbrella; v4 can name refined effects. Functions without a policy have observed effect summaries but no additional purity restriction; unknown effects prevent proof completeness rather than becoming findings.
evaluation: Fortress derives direct effects from structured PSM reads, mutations, external calls, reachable exceptional sites, and unsafe declarations, then computes deterministic call-graph fixed-point closure and checks the supported set against the authored policy.

finding.message: A supported direct or transitive function effect is forbidden by its authored policy.

remediation: Remove or isolate the effect, route it through an explicitly effectful boundary, or correct the authored policy when the effect is genuinely part of the function responsibility.
valid_example: A read-only query policy admits receiver_state_read and its supported call closure contains no other effect.
invalid_example: A function allowing only receiver_state_read directly or transitively mutates the receiver or performs an external interaction.
exception_policy: Opaque and unsupported effects remain uncertainty and do not become PASS. No exemption exists for a forbidden effect Fortress proves within the supported closed vocabulary.
history: Introduced with Function Contract v3 and deterministic transitive effect summaries.
